title: question about FAB assets
author: Vleaides
selftext:
Howdy folks. ive been building a game on and off as a hobby since 2021ish in unreal engine. however i recently had huge jumps in progress since I started using ai. (To clarify, ive only used it for the coding and not much else. I was intending to buy assets from fab or get them custom made via artists. also idm if i lose money, i love working on this project and making something id really enjoy, idk yet if I ever will publish the game but who knows). 

now here's the thing ive noticed that fab has listed on its asset pages that the creator does not allow the model to be used with generative ai usage. googling suggest that since ai is only being used in the coding, using fab assets would be fine. but i am not sure, can anyone confirm if fab assets are OK to be used? or what sort of limits are there?

thanks in advance

comments.author: CommercialInvite2810
comments.body: So I happen to be pretty much the opposite. I'm not a coder. I have played more around with the AI for content creation. I started building a game using just ai and rust. So far so good. It's been fun. I don't know if it's what you're looking for but look into rust. It's different for sure. Lot less overhead. I don't know. I've been having fun doing it. It's all open sources and becoming more and more compatible. It's just the way it's written. You'll know if you have errors right away. I won't let you move forward basically without having it correct and it's just better for me. It made me want to write my own programs for everything for my computer without the bloat

replies.author: Vleaides
replies.body: what engine do you code with rust in? Im familiar with rust and it would certainly be so much easier than c++

replies.author: CommercialInvite2810
replies.body: Rust paired with Bevy It doesn't have a visual encoder overhead. I was building a physics engine from scratch but it's amazingly small to compile and can run pretty much on anything. I could run it on a TV with a USB. I'm not finished with it yet, but it's a good example. And again, I'm not a coder. I can't remember exactly what it's called, but you don't have to worry about things having hooks in things. It runs a checker instead and also up front tells you if there's a problem. So if you're using AI which I do because I don't remember all the coding nuance if you get something wrong rust lets you know right up front. You don't have to wait to find out later and the zero bloat I got so tired of python which I still use for comfy UI and face fusion. I built multiples from the ground up but I want to rebuild both of those. I would love to rebuild them in rust face. Fusion is probably going to be my first. Just build my own for my computer

replies.author: CommercialInvite2810
replies.body: I forgot to say truthfully. My best selling point for me is my python environment for my comfy UI is 98,000 plus files. I think it's 110,000 now. Physics engine is one. I have notes and I have the programming I'm using to build it but in the end it's going to be one file. I think two maybe because I have to put the compatibility for different hardware but that's it

replies.author: Vleaides
replies.body: whats difference with physics engine to a normal engine? and also why? is it just for your personal use in game dev or hobby or is there some benefit im not understanding?

replies.author: CommercialInvite2810
replies.body: For me it was the bloat and the gamified part of it. I couldn't find one that doesn't have lives. Doesn't have a purpose. Doesn't have locks behind paywalls or that kind of stuff. This would be fully open. There's no life to die. There is no stopping walk under the ocean. If you want to physics still apply and I want it to be shiftable so that you can have sliders that shift and change how things work. You can make wood into water whatever the properties of it. Basically full freedom using some of the mechanics from tears of the Kingdom which was a killer way to do it. But they still have all the bloat of the entire storyline in the world and everything else that goes along with it to truly build one that is just open. It's very small in comparison. Also, you can have it generate unlimited scenery based on some parameters that way it doesn't have floating rivers or a house sticking out the side of the hill and then not tying the items to the physics so they can be separate. Basically it's a game that you could save a file and hand it to your buddy and it would be the exact same on yours as it is on his. Have it grab the hardware spec up front so it knows how many pieces to spawn so it doesn't go overboard that way. It's not always asking for memory, there's just a lot to it the other. I've never found anything like it for sure. Also compatible with almost any hardware

replies.author: CommercialInvite2810
replies.body: That is based on real physics at the baseline real gravity real shear strength, but you could slide the gravity up to 10,000 if you want. It'll crush everything instantly and you'll be done, but you can do it. Then you could spawn a new instance right there on the spot. Anyway, just a project. Something fun

comments.author: Wobblucy
comments.body: Point is they don't want their models getting fed into training data for the generative AI pieces.

replies.author: Vleaides
replies.body: ai cant access the unreal engine tho ? at least how im using it, whats the limit here? should I just avoid it at all costs?

comments.author: PocketStudio
comments.body: You should be fine, no need to avoid them. On NoAI listings the license bars using the assets in datasets for generative AI, in developing it, or as training inputs to it. Having AI write your game code is none of those. Epic staff confirmed on their forum in October that the EULA wording is what binds. The one thing I'd check: if your coding tool can read project files, make sure your provider doesn't train on them.

replies.author: Vleaides
replies.body: oh thats awesome. I dont believe ive given claude access to my files but since im using the desktop app, its best to check. thank you. any chance link where epic said this too?
